brief.headline: Push for 45-day payment terms (freeing ₹5.36 L cash for us) and line up a second source — they're 100% reseller with weak money-health (2/10) and pending legal cases.

priceAsk.summary: Hold current price but clarify maker's cost; probe for ₹0.65–0.80/pc on high-volume caps
priceAsk.target: ₹0.65–0.80/pc on 28 mm caps at higher volume
priceAsk.basis: Market asking price for these caps is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc — modest room to ₹0.65–0.80 at bigger orders or looser specs. Because they're 100% traders (0.0% manufactured, 100.0% traded), their price includes a reseller margin; ask them to share the maker's price so we can benchmark fairly.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days after receipt to 45 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹5.36 L cash for us (the full 30-day float at our ₹65.27 L annual spend).

brief.financialLeverage: They keep only 2.8% profit on each sale (peer average 3.1%), so they run tight. But they already pay their own suppliers in 105 days — much slower than similar firms (57 days) — which means they're used to stretching cash. We're 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue, a real chunk, so they'll listen. Their money-health score is 2/10 and they sit in the grey zone (Altman Z 1.58), with pending legal cases — push hard on terms and a second source, but avoid a huge price cut that could break a fragile supplier.

evidence.point: They're entirely a trader, carrying reseller margin in the price
They already take much longer to pay their suppliers than peers
We're a significant customer to them
They sit in financial grey zone with legal risk
evidence.figure: Altman Z 1.58 (grey zone), pending legal case(s)

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; a strong, qualified second source.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pharma (pails, containers, bottles/closures) — robust and profitable alternate.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ): manufacturer, India-wide presence, medium confidence — could be upstream resin or finished packaging source.

risks: Money-health 2/10 and grey-zone finances (Altman Z 1.58) with pending legal cases — supply continuity is at risk; don't concentrate all volume here.
They're 100% traders, so any price negotiation needs the maker's cost to benchmark fairly; without it we're guessing at the margin stack.
Only 2.8% profit margin — a heavy price squeeze could tip them into losses and hurt our supply; win on payment terms and volume commitments instead.
We have no internal price benchmark (ourAvgPrice, bestPriceWePay both null) — we're flying blind on whether ₹65.27 L annual spend is fair; urgently need a second quote to triangulate.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, and to keep growing our ₹65.27 L spend with you we need two things: 45-day payment terms — since you already pay your suppliers in 105 days — and visibility into the maker's price so we can plan fairly.
